rationale: Check round for CR-001 (missing spec 5.2 auditor test coverage). The fix-up diff is test-only (7 test files touched, no production code changed) and closes all five sub-gaps CR-001 named: (1) the project_admin_or_admin_user_detail_access auditor fast-path (gates GET /v1/admin/users/{id}) now has test_user_detail_access_auditor plus test_user_detail_access_auditor_skips_db_query verifying the pre-DB-query placement; (2) GET /v1/admin/users (list) now has test_auditor_sees_full_user_list asserting a non-empty 3-row result plus the route added to the dependency-wiring parametrize; (3) GET /v1/projects/{name}?include_spending=true now has a dedicated test asserting response.spending is populated (current_spending == 100.0), not just include_spending=False; (4) pure-auditor 403 write-rejection is now covered for /v1/project-budgets writes (walks the actual wired maintainer_access_only dependency per route) and for project update/delete (_authorize_project_access via the real, unmocked Ability check, plus ProjectService.update_project's is_admin_or_maintainer gate) — project create was deliberately left uncovered by design: create_shared_project has no admin/write gate for any caller (verified in source), so a 403 assertion there would be false, not a gap; (5) the PUT /v1/admin/users/{id} is_auditor assignment now has a router-level end-to-end forwarding test (test_update_user_forwards_is_auditor) parametrized across admin and maintainer callers, complementing the existing generic admin_access_only guard-function tests that already prove auditor-only gets 403 (that guard is FastAPI-Depends-injected and only actually executes at that boundary, so testing it directly is the correct level, not a duplicate). All touched test files (268 tests total) pass, and `make ruff` is clean. No new high-risk issue is plausible from a test-only diff, so no confirmation-pass dispatch was needed.
